questions.text: Why can a standard RNN not compute all hidden states across a sequence simultaneously during training?

options.A: Each hidden state must have a different vector dimension.
options.B: Each hidden state depends on the preceding hidden state.
options.C: Each input token must use a separately trained weight matrix.
options.D: Each input token must attend to all future input tokens.

questions.explanation: The recurrence h_t = f(h_(t-1), x_t) creates a dependency chain along the sequence.

questions.text: An implementation explicitly stores a dense attention score matrix for a sequence of N tokens. If the sequence length doubles while other dimensions stay fixed, how does the number of score entries change?

options.B: It grows by a factor of two.
options.C: It grows by a factor of four.
options.D: It grows by a factor of eight.

questions.explanation: A dense score matrix has N squared entries; (2N) squared is four times N squared.
The recurrence gives h=2.0 then h=0.9*2+4=5.8; the mean is (2+4)/2=3.0. These toy functions compute different quantities.
